evidence.title: Biomarker-Based Eligibility for Lung Cancer Screening: Validation of the Protein-Based INTEGRAL-Risk Model.
evidence.finding: Compared with questionnaire-based approaches, the protein-based INTEGRAL-Risk model improved short-term prediction of lung cancer in people with a smoking history. This model has potential to improve selection of high-risk individuals who are most likely to benefit from lung cancer screening.

evidence.title: Low-dose CT Screening and Smoking Cessation: Separate and Joint Associations with Mortality among Ever-Smokers Eligible for Lung Cancer Screening.
evidence.finding: For screening-eligible current smokers, recent quitting was associated with substantially larger reductions in LC and all-cause mortality than those associated with LDCT screening. These findings reinforce the importance of integrating effective smoking cessation interventions into LCS programs.

evidence.title: Occupational Exposure to Asbestos-Free Talc and Risk of Respiratory Cancers, Including Larynx, Lung, and Mesothelioma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.finding: Current evidence does not support increased risks of lung, mesothelioma, or laryngeal cancers among workers exposed to asbestos-free talc. Future studies should better control for confounders, especially tobacco smoking.

evidence.title: Development and Validation of a Blood Test Informed Risk Prediction Model for Lung Cancer-The Copenhagen Lung Cancer Risk Model (CPH-Lung).
evidence.finding: After inclusion of blood test information, the CPH-Lung model was more sensitive in the Danish population than PLCOm2012 for prediction of 6-year lung cancer risk particularly among women and younger individuals.

evidence.title: Validation of the Sybil Lung Cancer Risk Prediction Model in a Predominantly Black Screening Cohort: A Brief Report.
evidence.finding: Sybil reported robust lung cancer risk prediction in this screening cohort, supporting its generalizability and highlighting its potential to improve risk-based screening beyond the current eligibility criteria in diverse populations.

evidence.title: Gene-Specific Analysis of Clonal Hematopoiesis Identifies the Association Between ASXL1 and Lung Cancer Risk.
evidence.finding: Collectively, our findings support a model in which smoking-associated expansion of ASXL1-mutant clones is associated with an increased risk of lung cancer and suggest that gene-specific CHIP metrics may enhance risk stratification and early detection strategies.

evidence.title: Cytisine for Smoking Cessation Within a Lung Cancer Screening Program: Results From the Italian RISP Trial.
evidence.finding: This is the largest analysis of cytisine use within an LC screening program, providing supportive evidence of its potential effectiveness and safety profile, including in adults aged 65 years and older.

evidence.title: Smoking Cessation Among Underserved Patients Referred for Lung Cancer Screening: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.finding: Among medically underserved adults who currently smoked cigarettes and were referred for lung cancer screening, rates of sustained tobacco abstinence were higher through 6 months with addition of financial incentives compared with ask-advise-refer alone or with addition of free pharmacotherapy. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04798664.

evidence.title: Development and Implementation of an Integrated Early Lung Cancer Detection Program in Ethiopia: A Scalable Framework for Resource-Constrained Settings.
evidence.finding: Integrated early LC detection is achievable in resource-constrained settings when approached as a systems-level effort emphasizing phased infrastructure development, local adaptation, and pathway integration. These lessons provide a practical framework for LMIC implementation.

evidence.title: Biological aging and generational shifts in early-onset cancer risk.
evidence.finding: Greater age gap, reflecting more advanced biological aging relative to chronological age, may serve as a driver associated with risk of early-onset solid cancers, highlighting the importance of uncovering underlying mechanisms to guide effective prevention strategies.

evidence.title: Large-scale esophageal cancer screening through noncontrast computed tomography and artificial intelligence.
evidence.finding: Chictr.org.cn identifier: ChiCTR2300074806 .

evidence.title: Brief Report: Characterization of the Potentially Actionable TP53 Y220C Mutation in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer. A Multicenter, European Thoracic Oncology Platform Study.
evidence.finding: The TP53 Y220C has a frequency similar to other low abundance, actionable alterations in NSCLC. Patients with NSCLC should be screened and included in future trials of Y220C reactivators. Co-mutations in TP53 should also be analyzed, since they might be associated with intrinsic resistance.

evidence.title: Obesity Promotes Lung Carcinogenesis Through Airway Immune Dysfunction.
evidence.finding: Obesity is associated with enhanced lung carcinogenesis. Mechanisms of immune suppression up-regulated with excess adiposity, including activated, functional regulatory T cells, are evident in clinical and preclinical systems. These results challenge the concept of an obesity paradox regarding lung cancer risk.

evidence.title: Endobronchial Ultrasound-Guided Biopsy-Derived Lung Cancer Models: A Platform for Precision Therapy.
evidence.finding: EBUS-PDO and -xenograft‒derived organoids are good options to generate stable organoids in patients with advanced stage lung cancer. The models were consistent with the genetic and pathologic features of patient tumors, and the patient's responses to treatment, supporting their utility for novel therapeutic research.

evidence.title: Clinicogenomic determinants of early progression on first-line osimertinib in EGFR-mutant NSCLC.
evidence.finding: In this multicenter real-world cohort, baseline PD-L1 and TP53 combined with TSG predict very-early progression to first-line osimertinib, with EGFR subtype-specific prognostic impact of genomic co-alterations.

evidence.title: Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial.
evidence.finding: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05247684 .

evidence.title: Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy Versus Surgical Resection for Early-Stage Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: An Emulated Target Trial.
evidence.finding: This emulated target trial found higher 3-year all-cause mortality after SABR versus surgery in early-stage NSCLC suitable for either modality, supporting that surgical resection should remain the preferred option. The findings support SABR as a curative-intent alternative, particularly for older people.

evidence.title: Genomic Landscape and Clinical Impact of MTAP Loss in Driver-Positive NSCLC: Insights From a Large-Scale Real-World Chinese Cohort.
evidence.finding: MTAP loss defines a distinct molecular subset of NSCLC and serves as a robust adverse prognostic biomarker in EGFR-mutant disease treated with targeted therapies. These findings support integrating MTAP status into risk stratification and exploring combination strategies that incorporate PRMT5 or MAT2A inhibition.

evidence.title: Adaptive Feedback Signaling Through the FAK/SRC Pathway Promotes KRAS G12C Inhibitor Resistance.
evidence.finding: These data highlight the therapeutic potential of FAK/SRC inhibitors to mitigate adaptive signaling induced by KRAS inhibition and enhance the clinical activity of KRAS inhibitors.

evidence.title: Brief report: Clinical and Functional Characterization of Rare Germline and Somatic EGFR Variants in Three Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
evidence.finding: Broadening germline testing and functional variant characterization may enhance risk prediction and targeted therapy for individuals with NSCLC.

evidence.title: KEYNOTE-867: A Phase III, Randomized, Double-Blind Study of Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy With Pembrolizumab for Unresected Stage I or II Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
evidence.finding: The addition of pembrolizumab to SBRT did not improve EFS and was associated with a higher incidence of treatment-related AEs compared with SBRT alone in participants with inoperable stage I or II NSCLC. Based on the benefit-risk profile, the KEYNOTE-867 trial was prematurely stopped, and all study treatment was discontinued.

evidence.title: Induction and consolidation atezolizumab with stereotactic body radiation therapy versus radiation alone in high-risk, early-stage non-small-cell lung cancer (SWOG/NRG S1914): a multicentre, open-label, superiority, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.
evidence.finding: In the first fully reported phase 3 cooperative group trial to assess immunotherapy in inoperable early-stage NSCLC, we observed no improvement in overall survival with atezolizumab plus SBRT, and more grade 3 or higher adverse events were reported with atezolizumab combined with SBRT. FUNDING: US National Institutes of Health, US National Cancer Institute, and Genentech.

evidence.title: ctDNA-Based MRD Detection in Stage III NSCLC Treated With Chemoradiotherapy and Durvalumab.
evidence.finding: Detectable ctDNA during and after durvalumab was associated with markedly shorter PFS in unresectable stage III NSCLC. Serial ctDNA-based MRD assessment may help identify patients at high risk of relapse who could benefit from alternative or intensified treatment strategies, ideally within prospective clinical trials. GOV IDENTIFIER: NCT04392505.

evidence.title: Thymic Composition Predicts Radiation Pneumonitis in Locally Advanced NSCLC.
evidence.finding: pTT is an interpretable, host-specific radiographic biomarker associated with severe pneumonitis after cCRT in NSCLC. Incorporating pTT into risk stratification may improve individualized treatment planning and support the safer delivery of curative-intent therapy in locally advanced NSCLC.

evidence.title: Segmentectomy Versus Lobectomy in NSCLC With Pathologically Invasive Features: A Post Hoc Supplementary Analysis of Multicenter, Phase 3 Trial JCOG0802/WJOG4607L.
evidence.finding: Segmentectomy demonstrated better OS compared with lobectomy even for NSCLC harboring pathologically invasive features. However, the risk of locoregional relapse after segmentectomy should be considered.

evidence.title: Emerging Targeted Therapies for HER2-Mutant NSCLC.
evidence.finding: Then, we summarize the clinical and preclinical evidence of HER2-targeted therapies and provide a forward-looking perspective of the treatment landscape of HER2-mutant NSCLC.

evidence.title: Osimertinib With or Without Chemotherapy in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer With EGFR and Concurrent TP53 Mutations: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.finding: In this randomized clinical trial, osimertinib plus chemotherapy significantly increased progression-free survival among patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC harboring concurrent TP53 mutations. These findings provided a clinical rationale for individualized combination strategies in the management of patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT0469

evidence.title: Pulmonary Nodules.
evidence.finding: Optimal overall management balances timely diagnosis in persons who have cancer with the avoidance of unnecessary invasive procedures in persons who have benign disease.

evidence.title: Integrating Histologic Descriptors Into the Ninth Edition TNM Staging Improves Prognostic Stratification of Lung Adenocarcinoma.
evidence.finding: These findings demonstrate that key histologic descriptors-including histologic grade, LVI, and STAS-represent robust and consistent prognostic parameters. Importantly, these descriptors provide complementary, stage-dependent information that may enhance risk stratification and inform refinement of future TNM staging frameworks, including the forthcoming tenth edition.

evidence.title: LAMPAD: An Integrated Circulating Tumor DNA-Based Model for Predicting Potential Cure in Patients With Resected NSCLC.
evidence.finding: Overall, the LAMPAD model outperforms single-time point postoperative ctDNA detection by effectively discriminating true negative patients, thereby offering a more reliable prognostic tool for identifying low-risk patients with potential for cure.

evidence.title: Pulmonary Toxicities of Antibody-Drug Conjugates in SCLC and NSCLC: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
evidence.finding: Pulmonary AEs are common and clinically meaningful in patients with lung cancer treated with ADCs. Pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease represents the key clinically actionable toxicity, with risk being influenced by tumor subtype and drug characteristics.

evidence.title: Prognostic Significance of Spread Through Air Spaces in Stage Ia/bN0 NSCLC-An Evaluation in the JCOG0802/WJOG4607L Clinical Trial Patients.
evidence.finding: These findings reinforce STAS and high-grade adenocarcinoma as clinically significant prognostic factors and support their incorporation into risk stratification for patients with stage IA (pT1a/bN0) NSCLC.

evidence.title: Adjuvant Nivolumab vs Observation in Resected Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.finding: Adjuvant nivolumab was not associated with improved disease-free survival in patients with resected non-small cell lung cancer without sensitizing EGFR and ALK alterations when given after planned adjuvant chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT02595944.

evidence.title: Tumor Mutational Burden as a Predictor of Immune-Related Adverse Events in Patients With Advanced NSCLC Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Brief Report.
evidence.finding: These findings indicate that a high TMB, particularly TMB more than or equal to the 19 mut/Mb, is associated with an increased risk and earlier irAE onset, independent of longer immunotherapy exposure. This association seems to be biologically driven by tumors enriched in CD8+ cells, supporting the role of elevated TMB as an irAEs biomarker.

evidence.title: Lung Cancer Patient Advocacy Progress and New Challenges Since 2006.
evidence.finding: Advocacy will continue to drive systems toward more patient-centered and equitable lung cancer care locally, nationally, and globally.

evidence.title: Brief Report: Intestinal Lymphangiectasia With Selpercatinib and Pralsetinib Treatment.
evidence.finding: Drug-induced IL occurs with selpercatinib or pralsetinib treatment. The frequency increases with longer drug exposure. Serial monitoring is essential and when necessary, dose modification. Most cases do not lead to treatment discontinuation.

evidence.title: ERBB2-Activating Mutations and Co-Occurring Genomic Alterations Contribute to Disease Heterogeneity in Patients With ERBB2-Mutant Lung Cancer.
evidence.finding: NSCLCs harboring ECD-ERBB2 mutations are associated with a unique clinico-genomic phenotype and improved outcomes with first-line chemoimmunotherapy. These findings have implications for optimizing treatment strategies in this disease.

evidence.title: Consensus Statement on ctDNA Minimal Residual Disease Testing in Early Stage NSCLC: A Delphi Study by the Asian Thoracic Oncology Research Group.
evidence.finding: These consensus recommendations provide a pragmatic framework to guide the responsible integration of MRD testing into clinical research and practice.

evidence.title: Disease Kinetics and Practice Patterns in More Than or Equal to 4-Year Long-Term Beneficiaries of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors for Advanced NSCLC.
evidence.finding: LTBs without progression at 4 years achieved durable control, with lung cancer-specific OS approaching 90% at 8 years of follow-up. Late progression is uncommon, limited in extent, and often treated locally. The predominance of non-lung cancer-related mortality underscores the importance of comprehensive survivorship care.

evidence.title: Impact of Genomic Subtype on Intracranial Outcomes in Treatment-Naive, EGFR-Mutant NSCLC With Osimertinib (IGnITE).
evidence.finding: Patients with atypical and L858R EGFR mutations had significantly worse CNS outcomes compared with those with exon 19 deletions. Upfront SRS reduced the risk of CNS progression, with the greatest benefit in patients with atypical alterations. EGFR subtype may help identify patients who benefit from SRS.
